name: Morphological Gradient
description: Analyzes the morphological gradient (dilation minus erosion) for edge structure analysis. AI images show different edge morphology patterns.
mechanism: Computes morphological dilation and erosion operations and analyzes resulting gradient features for edge structure differences.
source: Serra (1982), Image Analysis and Mathematical Morphology
useCase: Detecting edge morphology differences in AI-generated content
strengths:
• Robust edge detection through dilation-erosion operations
• Less sensitive to noise than derivative-based methods
• Captures edge thickness and regularity
• Simple mathematical foundation
• Effective for detecting over-smooth AI boundaries
limitations:
• Structuring element shape affects results significantly
• Cannot capture fine-grained texture details
• Binary morphology loses grayscale information
• Computationally expensive for large kernels
• AI-generated edges increasingly realistic

references.title: Serra, J. (1982). Image Analysis and Mathematical Morphology. Academic Press.
Soille, P. (2003). Morphological Image Analysis: Principles and Applications. Springer.
Haralick, R.M. et al. (1987). Image Analysis Using Mathematical Morphology. IEEE TPAMI.
